description:
The verify cache reuses a GREEN verdict and re-earns a RED one, so an agent that cannot fix a gate pays the ENTIRE gate again on every iteration to be told the same thing. Measured on cuneiform, 2026-09-03.

THE LINE. `engine/lib.sh:215`, inside `verify_cache_try`:

    [ "$(sed -n 's/^status=//p' "$rec" | head -1)" = 0 ] || return 1

The key is already exactly right for this — `tree.base.hook`, built one line above from `git rev-parse HEAD^{tree}`, the base sha and `git hash-object "$VERIFY_HOOK"`. A record under that key is a statement about a SPECIFIC tree gated by a SPECIFIC hook against a SPECIFIC base. If the tree has not moved, the hook has not changed and the base has not changed, the gate is a deterministic function of those three and its verdict cannot have changed either. The cache already trusts that reasoning completely for `status=0`. It discards it for every other status.

WHAT IT COST. `cuneiform:388-the-panel-emission-contract` ran from 01:55 to 07:52 and merged nothing. Its log holds FIVE full gate runs (`grep -c 'verify: gating 28 changed file'`), and SIX identical failures:

    ✗ verify: gate "engine-build" FAILED (selected by changed path
      core/engine/assets/render-templates/_mcp/mcp_server.py.j2) — blocking merge

Every one of them was the same single assertion in `render_tool_extension_payload_contract.rs`. Between them the agent wrote, in its own words, 'All four stories read `passes: true` … Nothing left to implement this iteration.' It had nothing to change, changed nothing, and the tree was therefore BYTE-IDENTICAL across those runs — the exact case the key was designed to recognise.

One of those gate runs costs 11.6 minutes of test execution in that repo (summed from the log's own `finished in` lines, one run: 697.8s). Four of the five were re-derivations of a verdict already on disk. That is ~46 minutes of the ~6 hours, spent proving a known red verdict four more times.

WHY THIS IS NOT THE FLAKY-TEST ARGUMENT. The objection to caching a failure is that a red verdict may be noise, and re-running is how noise gets shaken out. That objection applies to re-running the same gate after SOMETHING CHANGED — a different tree, a moved base, an edited hook — and in every one of those cases the key already changes and the cache already misses. It does not apply here: nothing changed, and a second identical run is not a second sample of a flaky test, it is the same computation. An escape hatch belongs in the design anyway, and the operator must be able to reach it.

WHAT THIS IS NOT. It is NOT the double-verify `117` fixed (that was running a verify whose verdict was already recorded THIS iteration) and NOT the invisibility `119` fixes (a long verify reading as a hang). Those two make one gate run cheaper and legible. This one stops the gate running at all when its answer is already known. All three were visible in the same 6-hour window and none of them subsumes another.

userStories.title: A recorded verdict is reused whatever its status
userStories.notes: Reuse is now status-agnostic; the key is the whole argument and does not become false when the answer is red. verify_cache_try returns the RECORDED exit status on a hit and 1 on a miss ($VERIFY_CACHE_HIT tells them apart) — chosen in that direction so a caller ignoring the flag re-runs a red hit (wasteful, never wrong) rather than skipping the gate and accepting a failing tree. verify_cache_output replays the retained report; verify_cache_record retains the tail (500 lines) of a RED gate's output as <key>.out, pruned together with its record, and all three writers feed it (agent boundary tees, driver pipes via the new `-` stdin mode, chief verify tees). THE KEY ALSO GREW A FOURTH COMPONENT, because reusing a red exposed a latent hole in the three-part one: a project worktree never initializes its submodules, so the agent boundary runs the hook with dep/ an EMPTY DIRECTORY while the merge phase runs submodules_sync first (93) and runs the same hook over the same tree against a synced submodule — same tree sha, same base, same hook, different filesystem. OBSERVED: with the three-part key, test/submodule-gitlink.sh went red — 'A: expected MERGED, got VERIFY-FAILED', the worker log showing the merge phase replaying the boundary's legitimate 'submodule working tree is STALE' verdict instead of re-running the check, 3 attempts of 3, reproduced twice standalone. The key now carries a cksum of `git submodule status --recursive` ('nosub' where there are none, so a submodule-free repo is unchanged), and the same test PASSES. OBSERVED, test/verify-cache.sh VERIFY-CACHE OK, 6 parts: PART A green reuse hook 1x; PART B moved tree 2x; PART C edited hook blob 3x; PART D red hook 4x and a SECOND identical iteration STILL 4x (the fix) with the log carrying 'RED verdict, exit 1, from <record>', the record path itself, the replayed 'fixture verify hook (RED) ran in ...' and 'agent verification failed' — agent exit non-zero BOTH times, so a reused red never reads as a pass; PART D's invalidation control moves the tree and goes to 5x; PART E the neutered-engine reproduction still 2x. TWO MUTATION CHECKS, both caught: restoring `[ "$st" = 0 ] || return 1` in verify_cache_try fails PART D with 'THE RED SKIP DID NOT HAPPEN — the hook ran 5x, expected 4'; flipping the agent red-hit arm to `return 0` fails with 'A REUSED RED WAS ACCEPTED AS A COMPLETION'. GATES: bash -n clean on bin/chief + engine/*.sh + test/*.sh; shellcheck 0.11.0 -S error CLEAN on bin/chief, engine/lib.sh, engine/agent.sh, engine/driver.sh, test/verify-cache.sh (run via npx — not installed on this host, CI enforces it); quality ratchet OK (function_length_max 596 -> 602, delta +6 tol 15; single_use_functions 67 -> 67; duplicate_blocks 0 -> 0); check-doc-links 0 dead references; chief lint 2 tasklist(s) clean; doc-sync PASS (README + ROADMAP v0.9.17 == VERSION 0.9.17, 44 merged tasklists); version-bump PASS (0.9.17 covers every engine/bin change); behavioural smoke PASS, ratelimit PASS (3/3 standalone), noworkguard PASS, merge-batch PASS, verify-cache PASS, submodule-gitlink PASS, quality-ratchet PASS, cigate PASS. ALSO FIXED HERE, because US-1's change broke it: test/verify-stream.sh PART C is a REPRODUCTION that sed-restores the pre-119 command-substitution form in a copy of the engine, and its anchor was the exact line this story changed (the gate output is now tee'd into the record). It failed loudly — 'PART C: could not restore the command-substitution form — its anchor moved' — rather than passing quietly; re-anchored on the new pipeline, verify-stream now PASSES all 7 parts (A-F2) standalone. FINAL FULL GATE: `chief verify` exit 0, 'verify: OK (allowing merge)', recorded GREEN for tree c8fca3c907cb0e8174832b89b1db916130d19843 — the whole 60-test bystander block, quality ratchet, doc-links, VERSION-bump, doc-sync and tasklist-categories. Three earlier full-gate runs were red and each is accounted for: submodule-gitlink (the real defect above, fixed), then VERSION-BUMP (the follow-up engine commit re-staled 0.9.16 -> 0.9.17), then verify-stream PART C (above). Two additional bystander failures were LOAD flakes, not this change — ratelimit ('run exited non-zero' after '● rl finished -> MERGED', load 5.65 with two other repos' chief runs live) and merge-batch PART D ('the bisect did not isolate charlie as member #3 of 4'); each passed 2/2 standalone immediately afterwards and each passed inside a different full run.
acceptanceCriteria: `verify_cache_try` reuses a record whose `tree`, base and hook all match, REGARDLESS of its recorded status — a red verdict short-circuits to the recorded failure exactly as a green one short-circuits to success, and returns the recorded exit status to its caller.

The caller's behaviour on a reused RED is identical to a freshly-run red: `COMPLETE_OK` is set to 0 and completion is refused. A reused red must never read as a pass. Assert this over `_agent_verify_final` itself, not only over `verify_cache_try` in isolation — the bug this guards against is a status inverted on the way out.

The announcement line distinguishes the two: the green path keeps its existing `verify SKIPPED: … (GREEN verdict from …)` wording, and the red path says so in its own words, naming the record it came from. An operator reading a log must never have to guess whether a gate ran.

The recorded FAILURE OUTPUT is replayed, not just the status. A reused red that prints no reason leaves the agent with a blocked completion and no failing test named — which is the `119` invisibility bug reintroduced through a different door. If the current record does not retain enough output to do this, `verify_cache_record` is extended to retain it.

userStories.title: The operator can force a re-run
userStories.notes: CHIEF_VERIFY_CACHE=0 makes every verify_cache_try lookup decline, so the gate runs and its fresh verdict OVERWRITES the record — overwriting is free because every caller records after running, and it matters as much as bypassing: a hatch that only skipped the lookup would leave the disbelieved verdict on disk for the next un-hatched run. The check sits AFTER the record is located so the forced run names the verdict it is ignoring (">> verify cache DISABLED (CHIEF_VERIFY_CACHE=0): a matching verdict exists (<record>) and is being IGNORED"), because "the gate ran" and "the gate ran because you asked it to" are different log lines. The safety argument is written beside the code in engine/lib.sh: for a fixed tree, base, hook and submodule checkout the gate is a deterministic function of its inputs, so a second run is not a second sample; a gate for which that is false is one chief cannot detect from the outside (both runs are just a status), so the operator says so. Documented in docs/reference/verify-hook.md beside `chief verify`, in the same style as CHIEF_VERIFY_TESTS=0 / CHIEF_SWEEP=0 / CHIEF_MERGE_BATCH_BISECT=0. OBSERVED, test/verify-cache.sh VERIFY-CACHE OK, 7 parts: new PART F drives both directions over ONE red record and ONE unmoved tree — unset, the hook does NOT run (count held at 5, skip logged, completion still refused); CHIEF_VERIFY_CACHE=0, the hook RUNS (5 -> 6), the log carries "verify cache DISABLED", no SKIP, the completion is still refused, and a sentinel line planted in the record is GONE afterwards (status=1 re-recorded), proving replacement rather than bypass. The harness now UNSETS the variable for every other part instead of passing its default. TWO MUTATION CHECKS, both caught: neutering the hatch (`if false`) fails PART F with "THE HATCH DID NOT RE-RUN THE GATE — the hook ran 5x with CHIEF_VERIFY_CACHE=0 set, expected 6"; defaulting it to cache-off (`${CHIEF_VERIFY_CACHE:-0}`) fails PART A with "THE SKIP DID NOT HAPPEN — the hook ran 2x". GATES: `chief verify` exit 0, "verify: OK (allowing merge)", recorded GREEN for tree 3204c7202b6e92fddd8d64575f7d087fe22921e0 — BYSTANDER PASS (60 tests), quality ratchet OK (function_length_max 596 -> 602 tol 15, single_use_functions 67 -> 67, duplicate_blocks 15 -> 9), VERSION-BUMP PASS (0.9.18 covers every engine/bin change), DOC-SYNC PASS (README + ROADMAP v0.9.18 == VERSION, 44 merged tasklists), check-doc-links 0 dead references, tasklist-categories OK. shellcheck 0.11.0 -S error CLEAN on engine/lib.sh + test/verify-cache.sh (run via npx; not installed on this host, CI enforces it). One earlier full-gate run was red on test/teardown.sh and it was a LOAD flake, not this change (load average 15.26 on 14 cores with other repos' chief runs live) — it passed standalone immediately afterwards, all four parts, and passed inside this green run.
acceptanceCriteria: An explicit escape hatch re-runs the gate and overwrites the record even when a matching one exists — an env var in the same style as the rest of the engine's toggles, documented where the other toggles are documented.
The hatch is asserted by a test: with a red record present and the hatch set, the hook RUNS (drive a hook that appends to a file and assert the file grew); with it unset, the hook does not run.

A genuinely flaky gate therefore stays reachable, and the reasoning for why the default is safe — identical tree, identical base, identical hook is the same computation — is written down next to the code rather than only in this description.

userStories.title: The saving is demonstrated, not asserted
userStories.notes: The saving is a NUMBER now. test/verify-cache.sh PART G drives the incident end to end against a cache that has never held a verdict — its own repo ($WORK/repo-loop, so verify_cache_dir keys it to its own directory) with its own extra commit (so its tree sha differs from the scratch tree PARTS A-E recorded verdicts for, asserted before the first run), a RED hook, and a reset counter. Three iterations: nothing changes, nothing changes, then the tree moves. OBSERVED, test/verify-cache.sh VERIFY-CACHE OK, 8 parts (A-G): iteration 1 pays the gate 1x and refuses completion; iteration 2 pays it 0x — hook count HELD at 1 across both — refuses completion again, and its log carries 'RED verdict' and the replayed 'fixture verify hook (RED) ran'; iteration 3 commits and the gate runs again (1 -> 2). Three iterations, two gate runs. TWO MUTATION CHECKS, both caught, run against a standalone harness (everything above PART A plus the PART G block, into a temp dir beside a copied engine/) because PARTS A-F fail first under any mutation of this mechanism and PART G would never execute: restoring `[ "$st" = 0 ] || return 1` in verify_cache_try fails at 'iteration 1 paid the gate 2x, expected 1' — the saving starts INSIDE one iteration, since a red boundary verify sends the loop round for another turn over the same tree; flipping the agent's red-hit arm to `return 0` fails at 'iteration 1 accepted a completion over a red gate'. A third mutation (dropping `tree` from the key) is NOT caught by PART G and the comment says so: the fixture commits ON the base branch, so iteration 3 moves the tree AND the base — it asserts the KEY moved, not which half, and PART C is the component isolation. DOCS: new '### What a verdict is keyed on' in docs/reference/verify-hook.md — the four components in a table, one row per component giving the REASON it is in the key, the record/.out layout, the 32-record prune, and the status-agnostic reuse rule with the cuneiform measurement; the two places that still said `tree . base . hook` now name the four-part key and link the section, and '### Forcing a re-run' opens on the determinism assumption instead of re-stating the rule. ROADMAP's 117 row said the boundary 'tries the cache' and stopped, leaving green-only reuse reading as deliberate — it now names the status=0 limit as the first implementation's, points at 120 and at the doc. GATES: `chief verify` exit 0, 'verify: OK (allowing merge)', RECORDED GREEN for tree b8e2252d4de56ef82c03fc37a3c8488708dc476f, first attempt, no red runs and no flakes — BYSTANDER PASS (60 tests, including verify-cache with PART G and verify-stream), quality ratchet OK (no tracked metric regressed; duplicate_blocks 15 -> 9, single_use_functions 67 -> 67), VERSION-BUMP PASS (0.9.18 covers every engine/bin change; this story touches only test/ and docs/), DOC-SYNC PASS (README + ROADMAP v0.9.18 == VERSION, 44 merged tasklists), check-doc-links 0 dead vs 0 on main, tasklist-categories OK. bash -n clean; shellcheck -S error CLEAN on test/verify-cache.sh (run via npx; not installed on this host, CI enforces it).
acceptanceCriteria: A test drives the real loop shape that produced this: a hook that fails, an agent iteration that changes nothing, and a second iteration. Assert the hook is invoked ONCE across both, and that both iterations refuse completion.
A follow-up iteration that DOES change the tree re-runs the hook — the key moves, the cache misses. Assert this in the same test so the fix cannot be over-applied into a cache that never invalidates.

`docs/` records the cache's contract in one place: what the key is made of, why each of its three components is in it, and that the verdict is reused for any status. The `117` entry is updated to point at this rather than left implying green-only is deliberate.
